subject: Re: GovTech pilot onboarding — lightweight PO / allowlist approach
messages:
From: Luca Romano <luca@govtech.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@govtech.io
Date: 2027-10-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot onboarding — small scope, PO flexibility?

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the private deployment option. We're ready to run a 60-day pilot (up to $18K) with a handful of internal users, but procurement has flagged our standard PO requirement for vendor spend under $25K as an expensive friction for pilots.

Is Redwood able to support a short-term onboarding that doesn't require a PO but still gives us the audit trail and approvals procurement needs? They suggested either an invoice-only path (with a signed SOW and evidence of SOC2) or holding fees in escrow. Happy to share a brief SOW.

Luca
Product Lead, GovTech Solutions

--

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Luca Romano <luca@govtech.io>
Date: 2027-10-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding — small scope, PO flexibility?

Thanks Luca — looping in Marissa (on enterprise onboarding) and Karthik (finance approvals) to align. Short answer: we can do a conditional, invoice-first pilot for sub-$25K customers if certain controls are in place (signed SOW, vendor intake docs, minimum evidence). Escrow is uncommon for pilots but not impossible.

Proposed next steps:
- GovTech to sign SOW (you already attached the draft — thanks).
- Provide W9 + SOC2 or compensating controls.
- Fill our PO Exception Request form (we'll coordinate approvals).
- Redwood issues invoices on 30-day net for pilot usage; finance flags the account for expedited review.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm the approval path and whether we need a finance memo for escrow?

Sean
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-09T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding — small scope, PO flexibility?

Sean / Karthik — I recommend the invoice-only pilot with conditions instead of escrow: escrow introduces legal and payment OP complexity for <$25K and slows time-to-first-usage. Our standard practice for similar pilots is:

- Signed SOW with explicit pilot limits and termination clause.
- Vendor intake completed (W9/enterprise contact/terms accepted).
- SOC2 Type II OR a security attestation + temporary IP/PI guardrails in the SOW.
- PO Exception Request form routed to Finance + Legal for a one-off approval (we typically get a decision within 48-72 hours).

I can own the onboarding checklist and speed up intake. If procurement insists on escrow, send me the procurement contact and the exact language they need — we can evaluate, but we should present invoice-only first.

Marissa
Manager, Enterprise Onboarding
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: po-exception-request-form.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: FW: Pilot onboarding — finance check on invoice-only vs escrow

Grace — can you confirm whether Finance will approve invoice-on-net for a sub-$25K pilot if Legal signs off on the SOW and the PO Exception Request form is completed? If we need formal escrow language, what is the operational cost and SLA impact?

Key points:
- Customer is a public-sector org; procurement is often prescriptive.
- Pilot capped at $18K, single-month usage expected.
- We need to balance speed vs. our exposure.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot onboarding — finance check on invoice-only vs escrow

Team — Finance is comfortable with an invoice-first approach under the following controls:

1) Signed SOW that limits liability and includes a clear termination/cap cap.
2) Completed vendor intake (W9, remit address).
3) PO Exception Request (we need the completed form in the ticket).
4) Pre-authorization of a credit hold if invoices age >60 days.

Escrow: we'd only recommend escrow for long lead or multi-month prepayments >$50K. Operationally heavy for pilots (bank agreements, reconciliation) and would likely delay start by ~2 weeks.

If procurement insists on escrow, ask them to provide escrow instructions and bank details; Finance will review and provide an estimate for costs and timelines.

Grace
VP, Finance (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

I'll own the onboarding queue and keep things moving.

Best,
